properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/03/2023 to DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in Hayfield Twp, Crawford county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 981009
Permit API: 039-25416
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: Hayfield Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 369107 dated 12/30/2022.A complaint was emailed to the Department regarding a tank overflow of produced fluid from the 100bbl steel storage tank onsite.Upon arriving at the site, produced fluid was observed on the side of the tank, tank steps, and pooled within the earthen dike. Oil product was also observed to be on the side of the 50bbl poly tank and around the thief hatch of the tank. It appears that the 100bbl steel tank had overflowed and released approximately 15-20 gallons of produced fluid to the ground within the earthen dike. It appears that an unknown amount of fluid (oil) was scrapped up and put into the 50bbl poly tank. The released fluids were contained to the earthen dike.The operator was contacted via phone while still onsite. The operator was unaware of the extent of the release. It was stated that a small release of 1 gallon was reported internally and a claim that everything was cleaned up. Since the release was being contained to the earthen dike, the operator stated that a cleanup crew would be onsite first thing in the morning to cleanup the release.1/4/2022 (11:00am)I stopped at the site and visual cleanup operations were nearly complete. The impacted area within the dike was scrapped up with an excavator and placed into a dump truck. Fresh clean gravel was onsite to reclaim the inside of the earthen dike. The impacted material will be hauled to their shop for future disposal.A follow-up inspection will be conducted by the Department once cleanup is completed.Violations are cited.

properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: East Fallowfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 07/29/2020
Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. The well appears to be producing and is properly labeled. A vertical separator is located inside a stone dike that is lined. It appears that the lined-stoned dike is leaking collected stormwater through the dike. Water has channeled and traveled to the rock ditch located on the outside of the pad. This area should be monitored for potential releases/pollution from the separator and piping. A 210bbl steel tank is inside a lined containment.According to Scott Lux (DEP WQSS) the NOV's identified on 1/27/2020 for inspection #: 2988353 relating to the frac tank and release to the ground have been corrected. A new containment area has been installed with a 210bbl steel tank. Observations indicate that a release has occurred inside of the containment. Oil absorbent pads are floating inside the containment during the inspection. There are also several large areas, just outside on the north side of the secondary containment that were observed to indicate a release had occurred to the ground. The site has not been restored according to state regulations for restoration. The documents onsite all appear to be the original plans and documents. The Emergency Response Plan and PPC Plan should be reviewed and updated to reflect proper ownership/operator information.NOV's noted

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2018-12-03 to Cnx Gas Co Llc in Richhill Twp, Greene county. OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Cnx Gas Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2018-12-03
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 835628
Permit API: 059-27587
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-03
Comments: On December 3, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site, with Kevin Maskol (DEP). Present at time of inspection was Kyle Borden, Spencer Johnson, and Jason Harding (CNX). The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a incident inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites. At the time of the inspection the A, B, C, and D wells were being zipper fracked. The MASS was observed. It is located on a tank pad several hundred feet north of the well pad at an elevation of 1284. This is approximately 30' higher than the elevation of the well pad at 1253.5. It is not clear at this time if gravity had any effect on the incident. It was a 21K Bbl primary containment structure inside of a 24 K Bbl secondary containment structure. The tank manufacturer was Rain For Rent. This appears to match the approved OG-71B for the site. DEP recommends that CNX implement new engineering controls and operational changes to allow for emergency shut offs in the event of a release or other emergency during water transfer from an approved MASS to the frac.”

Comments: On 12/12/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the GH5 well site following an incident report submitted to the Department on 12/11/2023 (376984). I was accompanied by Andrew Perine of CNX. Additional representatives from CNX, Pine Belt Energy Services, and Penn E and R onsite.I contacted the operator on 12/11/2023 to follow up on the incident. The material involved was brine water. There is a pipeline off of CNX's GH 5 well site; the drip leg for the site was next to the pipeline and they believe that is the source of the spill. The leak is on the pad and goes downhill approximately 100 feet and is approximately 20 feet in width. The spill did not make it to the stream below. The stream downslope of the spill area is Lightner Run along Lightner Run Road. The operator was waiting for dumpsters to arrive on site at the time. They had the spill isolated and the clean-up crew from Pine Belt Energy Services is on-site. They roughly estimated the spill to be 84 gallons, however at that moment, they are unsure of the extent of the spill depth-wise. The operator is going to follow Act 2 guidelines and have their third-party crew analyze the site. The following was observed during inspection on 12/12/2023:Excavation of impacted material was occurring and waste placed into lined dumpsters. At the time, two barrels were estimated to have been excavated. The labels not updated to site - I recommend that the labels are updated (Photos 1, 2).Silt fence added below impacted area. I recommend that routine maintenance is performed on fence to ensure proper placement. Some parts of fence slumping (Photo 3).The impacted area was outline with orange paint (Photos 4-6). The area was approximately 80 feet in length and 12 feet in width further down slope (Photo 6). Closer to the well, another area was marked in orange and was approximately 20 feet in length (Photos 14-16, 25).Conductivity readings were taken within the impacted area. The noted readings ranged from 0.09 m/S - 19.29 m/S (specific locations noted in photo captions). Higher reading moving up the slope and in the area of origin near the well site (Photos 7-24). They estimated that the impacted material towards the bottom of the slope was around two inches in depth and deeper towards the top of the slope. Two feet were dug to reach the impacted material. There is a stream called Lightner Run that is on the opposite side of Lightner Run Road, below the impacted area. The road is approximately 335 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence and the stream is approximately 430 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence. Penn E and R is going to take samples within the stream.Due to the release of production fluid over a barrel, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: Site inspection at COP Tract 231 Pad A on August 28, 2020 with Rick Hall of ARD in regards to the spill reported earlier that morning. Prior to my arrival Mr. Hall was able to take some photos prior to the rain arriving. Mr. Hall's photos have been included in this inspection report. According to lease hand operator Matt Coppadge of ARD, he was manually dumping water from the dehydration unit to the produced fluids tanks via the 2" buried steel line. When Mr. Coppadge pressured back-up, he observed dust in the air and a wet spot on the surface of the well pad. He immediately stop pressurizing the line. When he assessed the well pad, he observed two holes on the surface of the well pad and a wet spot ~6-8 ft. in diameter. The release was later reported to the Department by Mr. Hall.When I arrived onsite, the well pad was wet due to the rain. Mr. Hall marked off impacted areas on the surface of the well pad based off soil screenings using a soil conductivity probe. I viewed the impacted area where the released had occurred. I screened the area using a soil probe. Soils/gravel right at the two holes on the well pad exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. As I moved away from the holes, readings decreased. Elevated soil readings were in an area approximate 6-8 ft. in diameter. An oil sheen was observed on the well pad near the holes and in a nearby puddle of water. The contractor arrived onsite the same time I did. In addition, Matt Lock of Tuscarora Geologic & Environmental Services arrived onsite prior to my departure. Mr. Lock will be collecting samples on behalf of ARD. Please note that is 2" buried steel dump line serves all three producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. ARD is currently unable to determine the amount of produced fluids released. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the site is required to be remediated under 78a.66 through the Act 2 process.Violations noted. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 35148

According to lease hand operator Matt Coppadge of ARD, he was manually dumping water from the dehydration unit to the produced fluids tanks via the 2" buried steel line. When Mr. Coppadge pressured back-up, he observed dust in the air and a wet spot on the surface of the well pad. He immediately stop pressurizing the line. When he assessed the well pad, he observed two holes on the surface of the well pad and a wet spot ~6-8 ft. in diameter. The release was later reported to the Department by Mr. Hall.When I arrived onsite, the well pad was wet due to the rain. Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 369107 dated 12/30/2022.A complaint was emailed to the Department regarding a tank overflow of produced fluid from the 100bbl steel storage tank onsite.Upon arriving at the site, produced fluid was observed on the side of the tank, tank steps, and pooled within the earthen dike. Oil product was also observed to be on the side of the 50bbl poly tank and around the thief hatch of the tank. It appears that the 100bbl steel tank had overflowed and released approximately 15-20 gallons of produced fluid to the ground within the earthen dike. It appears that an unknown amount of fluid (oil) was scrapped up and put into the 50bbl poly tank. The released fluids were contained to the earthen dike.The operator was contacted via phone while still onsite. The operator was unaware of the extent of the release. It was stated that a small release of 1 gallon was reported internally and a claim that everything was cleaned up. Since the release was being contained to the earthen dike, the operator stated that a cleanup crew would be onsite first thing in the morning to cleanup the release.1/4/2022 (11:00am)I stopped at the site and visual cleanup operations were nearly complete. The impacted area within the dike was scrapped up with an excavator and placed into a dump truck. Fresh clean gravel was onsite to reclaim the inside of the earthen dike. The impacted material will be hauled to their shop for future disposal.A follow-up inspection will be conducted by the Department once cleanup is completed.Violations are cited.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/07/2025 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Bell Township, Clearfield county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/07/2025
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8228096
Permit API: 033-24249
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/07/2025
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-24249 on April 07, 2025. The well site is well vegetated. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. The brine tank is stationed in an earthen dike. Several inches of standing fluids was observed in the earthen dike. I screened in the fluids and found elevated conductance 10.01 mS/cm (photo 5). I screened outside the earthen dike using a soil probe and found elevated conductance ranging from 1.28 mS/cm -1.86 mS/cm (photos 7-9). The impacted area outside the earthen dike based off my soil field screening is approximately 25' long x 15'. Please note, there is a stream located approximately 35 yards away from the brine tank. I screened the stream for specific conductance and got a field reading of 26.5 uS/cm (photo 11). I collected a grab sample from the standing fluids within the earthen dike (photo 12). The sample 3442852 will be sent away to the DEP Lab and be tested for SAC 0942 plus aluminum, bromide, and lithium. I notified Diversified ESH Specialist Will Warfel via phone at ~1445 of my findings. Violations have been cited. The Department recommends that the operator address remediation of the spill/release in accordance with policy 800-5000-001 (Addressing Spills and Releases at O and G Well Sites or Access Roads).

Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4014690 and violations issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a production fluid, frack chemical and fresh water mixture.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, there appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department did not observe the trench previously observed to be bordering the secondary containment in the release area during IR 4014690. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.75mS, 0.48mS, and 0.44mS . These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program.

Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. There was evidence of crude along the tributary to its confluence of Glad Run. An unknown amount of crude oil was released and made its way into waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On 8/26/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4237718, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. At the time of this inspection, no formal NOV Response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks. On 4/02/2026, Big Dog Energy representative Matthew Anderson responded via email to IR 4168852 and stated "As the DEP is aware this well was sold to Murphy Production in 2024. However in regards to the spill there was none. I ordered a new sign to put up just so this well can be transferred along with an ERP plan. Should have it within a week to install and get transferred to Murphy" (IR 4174382). However, the well site remained unchanged at the time of the previous inspection surface inspection, which was conducted on 7/15/2026 (IR 4237718).At the time of inspection, the following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (Photo 1). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (Photos 9 and 11). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (Photos 4-7). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (Photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (Photo 10). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (Photos 2 and 12).Based on todays inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4187078 remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken on site since the date of that inspection and no formal NOV Response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Violation ID: 8199416
Permit API: 129-23976
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2024
Comments: On August 21 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 Well in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the access road which remains unrestored. No active accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. Plugging operations appear to be completed. No equipment appears to be onsite and has been removed at the time of this inspection. The pit that was on site during plugging operations is now backfilled and is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the NOV response, which again included the requested Control and Disposal Plan, the Operator stated that:"The pit water was hauled away and used at another fracturing job by the contractor who was fracking in the area. The cement that was drilled out was encapsulated in the pit and buried. The Operator also stated that after one day, there was not water. That cement was created when we had to drill out and re-cement this well. The contractor that the Operator hired was confident that there is no water run off anywhere on location."However, under 25 PA Code 78.62(a)(1), disposal of residual wastes in pits may occur at the well site if the waste is generated by the drilling or production of an oil or gas well located on the well site. Additionally, under 25 PA Code 78.56(4)(d), pits used during servicing, plugging and recompleting the well shall be removed or filled within 90 days of construction. Therefore, the encapsulation of the residual waste and pit used during plugging of the well is not in compliance with 25 PA Code 78.62(a)(1) and 25 PA Code 78.56(4)(d). If the access road is to remain the Department requests the following information in regards to the access road:1. Map of area being proposing to remain including if there would PCSM proposed in that area.2. Map or overlay of how site was to be restored.3. Include property boundaries.The Department requests an NOV response to be provided to the Department by 9/4/2024. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding for failure to remove the pit. The well site and access road appear to be permanently stabilized at this time, violations are being closed for failure to implement Erosion and Sediment BMPs(Best Management Practices).
